record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Rank of average mixing matrix in primitive distance-regular graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with adjacency matrix A(G)=Σ_r θ_r E_r, and let its average mixing matrix be \hat{M}=lim_{T→∞}(1/T)∫_0^T M(t)dt = Σ_r E_r∘E_r, where M(t)=U(t)∘U(-t) and U(t)=exp(itA). For a primitive distance-regular graph G, prove that the rank of \hat{M} equals the number of vertices of G.

evidence.quote: The average mixing matrix is defined as \hat{M}=\lim_{T	o\infty}\hat{M}_{[0,T]}, and a straightforward calculation shows that if A(G)=\sum_{r=0}^{d}	heta_r E_r then \hat{M}=\sum_{r=0}^{d} E_r\circ E_r.
If G is a primitive distance-regular graph, show that the rank of \hat{M} is equal to the number of vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A=A(G)$. Write the spectral decomposition $A=\sum_{r=0}^{d}\theta_r E_r$, where $\theta_0,\dots,\theta_d$ are the distinct eigenvalues of $A$ and $E_0,\dots,E_d$ are the corresponding orthogonal spectral idempotents. For $t\in\mathbb{R}$, define the continuous-time quantum walk transition operator $U(t)=\exp(itA)$ and the (instantaneous) mixing matrix $M(t)=U(t)\circ\overline{U(t)}=U(t)\circ U(-t)$, where $\circ$ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. Define the average mixing matrix by
$$\widehat{M}=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}M(t)\,dt.$$
A direct calculation gives $\widehat{M}=\sum_{r=0}^{d}E_r\circ E_r$.

Recall that a connected graph $G$ of diameter $d$ is distance-regular if, for every pair of vertices $u,v$ at distance $i$, the number of vertices at distance $j$ from $u$ and distance $k$ from $v$ depends only on $i,j,k$. A distance-regular graph is called primitive if each of its distance-$i$ graphs (for $1\le i\le d$) is connected.

Prove that for every primitive distance-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, $\operatorname{rank}(\widehat{M})=n$.
artifact.category_tag: Average mixing matrix of quantum walks
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question on the rank of the average mixing matrix of primitive distance-regular graphs. Related work (e.g., Coutinho, Godsil and coauthors on the average mixing matrix and its rank) addresses general bounds and special families, but no general proof for all primitive distance-regular graphs has been located. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Research on connections between the rank of the average mixing matrix and graph structure.
status_evidence.claim: The rank of the average mixing matrix is an active topic; no general proof for primitive distance-regular graphs is reported.

status_evidence.title: A Quantum Walk Mixing Average Mixing Matrices (Godsil)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of average mixing matrices, with conjectures including that no primitive distance-regular graph of diameter three has certain rank-deficiency properties.
status_evidence.claim: Rank properties of the average mixing matrix for distance-regular graphs remain conjectural.
